sentences.text: Petitioner is the first accused in C.C. No.183 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Perumbavoor, arising out of Crime No.1984 of 2021 of Perumbavoor Police Station, registered for the offences under Sections 420 and 406 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Perumbavoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3rd respondent is the defacto complainant and 4 th respondent is the aggrieved person.

3. According to the prosecution, accused had cheated the defacto complainant and the 4th respondent by promising them a job at Canada and collected an amount of Rs.9,26,000/- and thereafter cheated them by failing to arrange visa or provide employment or return the money and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondents, apart from the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the matter has been settled and hence the proceedings against the petitioner ought to be quashed.
It was also submitted that, considering the nature of offences alleged, no purpose would be served by continuing the CRL.MC NO. 5993 OF 2024 2024:KER:75600 proceedings.

6. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303], the Apex Court has held that in appropriate cases, the High Court can take note of the amicable resolution of disputes between the victim and the wrongdoer to put an end to the criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This view was reiterated in Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [(2014) 6 SCC 466] and Yogendra Yadav and Others v. State of Jharkhand and Another [(2014) 9 SCC 653].
7.

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [(2014) 6 SCC 466]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Yogendra Yadav and Others v. State of Jharkhand and Another [(2014) 9 SCC 653]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have perused Annexure A2 and Annexure A3 affidavits filed by respondents 3 and 4.
The learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that upon verification, it is understood that the affidavits are genuine, and the defacto complainant and the other deponent stand by the contents thereof.
I am satisfied that the matter has been settled and no public interest is involved in this case.
There is no impediment for granting the prayer for quashing.
The continuance of the proceedings will only be an exercise in futility.
8. Accordingly, all proceedings against the petitioner in C.C. No.183 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Perumbavoor are quashed.
